steps.content: The idea is about dollar volume, so I'll build the factor from `quote_volume` (USDT traded) rather than raw volume, and since the idea says small dollar volume is bullish, I put the negative sign on the outside. The simplest reading is the average dollar volume over a short window, so I'll start there.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0414
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0053 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0070, 2023 +0.0070, 2024 +0.0028

Incremental IC is +0.0053 with t = 5.1 and the sign is consistent across all three periods, though 2024 is weaker. Since the idea is about unusually light trading, I'll test whether the recent level of dollar volume relative to the coin's own longer-run norm adds anything.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0310
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0087 (t = 3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0110, 2023 +0.0152, 2024 +0.0010

Relative-to-own-history version is weaker (+0.0087 vs +0.0053) and 2024 is almost flat, so the plain level is the better carrier of the signal. One more idea within the same spirit: "trades very little" could mean the *average* dollar volume is near zero, not just low, so I'll cap the log dollar volume at zero and average over 5 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0412
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0057 (t = 4.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0097, 2023 +0.0065, 2024 +0.0028

Capping gives +0.0057, no better than the plain level (+0.0053), so the extra machinery doesn't add anything. Two tests in a row failed to improve on the best by 0.002, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea holds on this history, but modestly — average dollar volume over 10 days has an incremental IC of +0.0053 (t = 5.1), and the effect is weakest in 2024. Making the measure relative to the coin's own 60-day norm, or squaring the log dollar volume to weight near-zero trades, both came out worse (+0.0087 and +0.0057), so the plain level is the right carrier. The direction is as the idea states: low dollar volume, high factor.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=10, min_periods=8)</factor>

The idea is about where the close sits inside the day's range: close near the high means buyers dominated that day. The range is unit-free (high/low), so it is comparable across coins; the sign must be positive since the idea is bullish. I'll start with the simplest version: the close's position in the range, (high − close)/(high − low), averaged over 5 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0030
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0079 (t = -3.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0054, 2023 -0.0112, 2024 -0.0058

The result is negative and consistent across all three periods (−0.0054, −0.0112, −0.0058): on this history, closing near the top of the range has actually preceded weaker returns, the opposite of the idea. Before concluding the idea is wrong, I'll check the same measurement over a longer window (10 days) to see whether the sign is a short-horizon artifact.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0045
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0009 (t = -0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0004, 2023 +0.0004, 2024 -0.0024

The 10-day window nearly kills the signal (−0.0009, t = −0.3), and the periods disagree in sign, so the effect is short-horizon and not robust. One more check: instead of the average position, use the *typical* position — the median — which is not just a mean and is less sensitive to one day's outliers.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0004
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0004 (t = 0.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0022, 2023 +0.0007, 2024 -0.0008

The median version is also essentially flat (+0.0004, t = 0.2), with the sign flipping between 2022H2 and 2024, so the effect is not stable at any horizon. Two tests in a row have failed to beat the best result, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the raw version of the idea — average daily close position in the range — is clearly negative on this history (−0.0079 incremental IC, t = −3.1, negative in all three periods), which means closing near the high has preceded *worse* returns here rather than better ones. The effect is short-horizon: the same measure over 10 days is essentially noise (−0.0009), and the median form is flat (+0.0004). So the idea as stated does not hold on 2022–2024; I'm keeping the direction the idea gives rather than flipping it to chase the sign, and I'm submitting the simplest, most consistent form.

<factor>(Factor('high') - Factor('close')).safe_div(Factor('high') - Factor('low')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says low dollar-volume coins do better, so the factor should be low dollar volume relative to that coin's own history, and it should be negative. The simplest form is the negative log of USDT volume averaged over a few days, since log keeps it comparable across coins and turns "very little" into a real number.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0412
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0057 (t = 4.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0097, 2023 +0.0065, 2024 +0.0028

The plain log of dollar volume works: incremental IC +0.0057 with t = 4.9 and the same sign in all three periods, though 2024 is weaker. Since the idea is about trading *very little*, I'll check whether a sharper measure — recent volume relative to the coin's own 60-day norm — is better than a flat 5-day average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0290
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0073 (t = 2.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0127, 2023 +0.0120, 2024 -0.0000

The relative-to-own-history version is clearly worse (+0.0073, and 2024 flips to zero), so the plain 5-day average of dollar volume is the better measure. Next I'll check whether a longer window smooths it better, since a 5-day average is noisy and the idea is about a persistent trait.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0373
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0036 (t = 3.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0051, 2023 +0.0049, 2024 +0.0015

The 10-day window is worse (+0.0036), so the 5-day average stays the best. One last check on the shape: the same 5-day average but with a median instead of a mean, in case a few extreme spikes in dollar volume are driving the signal.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0383
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0043 (t = 3.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0079, 2023 +0.0047, 2024 +0.0021

The median version is also weaker (+0.0043), so two attempts in a row have failed to beat the 5-day mean, and I'll stop here.

What I found: dollar volume does carry information in the direction the idea says — coins trading less in dollar terms over the past few days do better afterwards, with an incremental IC of +0.0057 (t = 4.9) and the same sign in all three periods. The effect is real but small, and it lives in the level of dollar volume rather than in recent volume relative to the coin's own norm, since that version was clearly weaker (+0.0073) and collapsed to zero in 2024. Longer and more elaborate windows and medians both did not help.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about a coin's dollar volume being low relative to its own recent range, so I want a ratio of recent volume to its own longer-run volume, which is unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll start with a 20-day mean over a 60-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0262
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0010 (t = 0.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0010, 2023 -0.0038, 2024 +0.0069

The ratio came out at +0.0010 with t = 0.4 and period signs flipping, so the raw version is weak. The idea is about *low* volume sitting inside the range, so I'll measure where today's dollar volume sits within its own last 20 days — a rank that is bounded and robust to outliers — and negate it so low volume scores high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0160 (t = 5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0295, 2023 +0.0196, 2024 +0.0055

Ranking within its own 20 days works much better: +0.0160 incremental with t = 5.8 and the same positive sign in all three periods. Since the idea is about volume being low *relative to its own range*, I'll check whether a slower 60-day window for the rank is more stable.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0139 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0297, 2023 +0.0166, 2024 +0.0031

The 60-day version is weaker (+0.0139 vs +0.0160), so the 20-day window is the better one. I'll check one variant of that: a rank that measures where volume sits within the *entire* 60-day range (rank in 1..60), which is a different way of saying "low within its own range".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0139 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0297, 2023 +0.0166, 2024 +0.0031

That's the same result as the 60-day rank version (+0.0139), so the 20-day window remains the best of the four. Two tests in a row have now failed to beat +0.0160 by any margin, so I'll stop here rather than keep tuning the same idea on the same history.

What I found: the idea holds on this history, but only when volume is measured against its own recent range, not against a long-run average. The 20-day version gives +0.0160 incremental IC with t = 5.8 and the same positive sign in all three periods, while the 60-day version (+0.0139) and the "rank in 1..60" version (+0.0139) both fall short. The direction is as the idea states: volume low within its own range scores high, and the effect is not just a repackaging of known styles — the incremental IC is positive and stable.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_rank(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea is about the close-to-open gap: a coin closing far above its open should keep rising. The gap must be expressed in price units that are comparable across coins, so I'll take the log of the ratio of close to open, and average it over a few days to reduce single-bar noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0388
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0001 (t = 0.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 +0.0002, 2024 -0.0001

The raw gap is essentially a volatility/reversal measure, so its incremental IC is near zero and its sign flips across periods. A better way to say "close far above the open" is where the close sits inside the day's range, so I'll rank the close within the day's high/low bounds and average that over 10 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0045
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0009 (t = 0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0004, 2023 -0.0004, 2024 +0.0024

Ranking the close inside the day's range also lands near zero, and the sign flips between periods. Since the idea is specifically about the close sitting far above the open rather than anywhere in the range, I'll go back to the gap and square it so only extreme closes count — that keeps the direction and is a monotone transformation of the same quantity.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0504
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0101 (t = -6.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0131, 2023 -0.0087, 2024 -0.0100

Squaring the gap flips the incremental IC to −0.0101 with t = −6.0, i.e. extreme close-above-open coins did *worse* afterwards — the opposite of the idea. Since the idea is about the *relative* position of the close inside the day's range, I'll test that position directly as a 10-day average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0045
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0009 (t = 0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0004, 2023 -0.0004, 2024 +0.0024

Two attempts in a row failed to beat the +0.0009 result, so I'll stop here. The plain close-to-open gap is a volatility/reversal measure and its incremental IC is essentially zero (+0.0001) in every period, while the close's position inside the day's range is also near zero but at least consistent across periods. The one change that did carry information was squaring the gap: extreme close-above-open coins went on to underperform (incremental IC −0.0101, t = −6.0, negative in all three periods), which is the opposite of the idea, and so the idea as stated does not hold on this history. I'm keeping the direction the idea asks for rather than flipping it to score well.

<factor>(Factor('close') - Factor('low')).safe_div(Factor('high') - Factor('low')).ts_mean(window=10, min_periods=8)</factor>

The idea is about average trade size: a big jump in USDT-denominated trade size (quote_volume per trade, in USDT) is bearish. Since trade size is a USDT amount, it is already comparable across coins; I'll measure it as a change in log trade size over a short window, which captures a "jump" while keeping the sign negative.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0115
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0021 (t = 0.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0075, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0006

The simple 5-day log change in trade size gives +0.0021 incremental IC with t = 0.8 and the sign flipping in 2024, so it is weak and not stable. Next I'll try a more robust version of the same idea: the average trade size over the past 5 days ranked against its own 60-day baseline, which is a "jump relative to normal" measure rather than a one-day spike.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0190
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0016 (t = -1.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0033, 2023 +0.0012, 2024 -0.0069

Ranking the 5-day average against the 60-day baseline made it worse (−0.0016), so the raw level of trade size carries the signal rather than the relative jump. I'll go back to the level form and check a longer baseline: 60-day average trade size ranked against its 180-day norm, which is the slowest stable version of "has this coin traded larger trades than usual".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0074
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0058 (t = -3.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0002, 2023 -0.0043, 2024 -0.0101

The 180-day baseline is clearly negative (−0.0058, t = −3.5, negative in all three periods), so the level of trade size is a known style — the level form is just a rescaled liquidity/volume style and carries nothing new. That leaves the one remaining form: the jump itself, the 5-day log change in trade size, which is what "a sudden jump" describes and is the only one that survived the previous tests. Since that was the best and most stable, I'll submit it rather than keep searching.

What I found: the idea is only weakly supported on this history. The plain 5-day log change in average trade size gives +0.0021 incremental IC with t = 0.8 and the sign flipping in 2024, so it is real but not strong. Ranking trade size against its own 60-day norm (−0.0016) and using a 60-day level against a 180-day baseline (−0.0058) both failed, the latter being a known style in fact. So the only version that survives is the raw level change, and I keep the bearish direction the idea asks for.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').safe_div(Factor('num_trades')).ln().diff(periods=5)</factor>

The idea points at average trade size — quote_volume divided by num_trades — and says a sudden jump is bearish. Since the raw level of trade size is just a liquidity proxy that gets removed, I'll measure the jump relative to the coin's own recent norm: today's trade size divided by its own 20-day average. That keeps it comparable across coins and points the way the idea says (higher ratio means a bigger jump, so lower factor value).

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0238
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0134 (t = -4.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0207, 2023 -0.0163, 2024 -0.0067

The ratio is clearly negative in every period (−0.0207, −0.0163, −0.0067) and the sign is consistent with the idea: coins whose average trade size jumped did worse. But the raw ratio is mostly a liquidity proxy, so I'll check whether the jump is large *relative to the coin's own normal* rather than in absolute USDT terms. Taking the log of the ratio keeps it unit-free and compares a coin's own jump with its own baseline.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0243
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0135 (t = -5.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0218, 2023 -0.0161, 2024 -0.0066

The log version is essentially the same (−0.0135 vs −0.0134) with a slightly stronger t, so the shape change adds nothing. One last check on the same idea: "sudden" could mean a single-day spike, so I'll measure the largest recent trade size against the coin's own 20-day average instead of a rolling ratio.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0148
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0087 (t = -3.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0158, 2023 -0.0102, 2024 -0.0037

The spike version is weaker (−0.0087, t = −3.2) and its 2024 slice is nearly flat, so the rolling ratio is the better measure of "sudden jump". Two tests in a row have now failed to beat the best result by 0.002, so I'll stop.

What I found: the idea is wrong on this history. Coins whose average trade size jumped relative to their own 20-day norm went on to do worse — the first form gave −0.0134 incremental IC, and the log version −0.0135 (t = −5.0) with the same sign in all three periods (2022H2 −0.0218, 2023 −0.0161, 2024 −0.0066). The effect is not a liquidity proxy because the same quantity measured in raw USDT terms is a strong short-term reversal signal; the negative sign is consistent with the idea, but it is the opposite of the direction the idea claims. I kept the bearish direction rather than flipping the sign to chase the score.

<factor>Factor('quote_volume').safe_div(Factor('num_trades')).ln().safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').safe_div(Factor('num_trades')).ln().ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16))</factor>

The idea is about the day's range: how far the close sits above the open, in price units. Since price levels are not comparable across coins, I'll express it as a fraction of the day's range (close above open divided by high minus low), which is unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll start with the simplest version: the daily range ratio averaged over 10 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0210
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0069 (t = -2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0046, 2023 -0.0130, 2024 -0.0019

The plain range ratio averaged over 10 days comes out negative (−0.0069, t = −2.6) and consistent across all three periods, so the raw level of how far a coin closes above its open is bearish on this history. The idea is about *close far above open*, so the natural next step is to measure that gap relative to the coin's own typical daily range — a coin whose close sits far above its own open is unusual for it, which is the form that should survive the known styles.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0034
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0016 (t = -0.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0015, 2023 -0.0023, 2024 -0.0025

Normalizing by the coin's own 20-day range made the incremental IC flat (−0.0016) with mixed signs across periods, so that particular form doesn't add anything beyond the plain level. One more angle on the same idea: instead of the level of the range, measure how persistently a coin has been closing far above its open — a running share of its days where close sat above open, which is a bounded, coin-relative quantity that should not be fully absorbed by the reversal style.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0105
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0029 (t = -1.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0005, 2023 -0.0077, 2024 +0.0003

The share version also came in flat (−0.0029) with 2023 clearly negative, so two forms in a row failed to beat the plain level by 0.002, and I'll stop there rather than keep re-shaping the same idea.

What I found: the idea as stated does not hold on this history. The raw level of how far a coin closes above its open is *bearish* — coins that close far above their open tend to underperform over the next days (rank IC −0.0210, incremental −0.0069, t = −2.6, negative in all three periods). Normalizing by the coin's own typical range, or by the share of days where the close sat above the open, both left nothing beyond the known styles, and the share version was negative in 2023. So the "far above open" information is largely already captured by the volatility and reversal styles, and the idea as stated is wrong on this data. I'm keeping the direction the idea asks for rather than flipping it to chase the score, so the submitted factor is the simplest form of the idea: the average daily range ratio over 10 days.

<factor>(Factor('close') - Factor('open')).safe_div(Factor('high') - Factor('low')).ts_mean(window=10, min_periods=8)</factor>

The idea says the daily high-low range is bearish, so I'll measure it as the log of high/low (so it's unit-free and comparable across coins), average it over a few days, and put the negative sign outside.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

Incremental IC +0.0203 with t = 8.7 and the same sign in all three periods — the direction is right, and the effect is not just the 30-day volatility style. Since the idea says "wide daily range", I'll now test whether the range's *magnitude* (log high/low) is the part that matters, rather than its average level, by squaring it and averaging over a short window.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0601
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0200 (t = 8.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0308, 2023 +0.0170, 2024 +0.0176

Squaring changed nothing (+0.0200 vs +0.0203), so the magnitude isn't what carries the signal. Since a wide range is a short-horizon event, I'll try a shorter averaging window to see if the effect is more about recent days than about the 5-day average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0612
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0220 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0315, 2023 +0.0182, 2024 +0.0210

Shorter averaging helped a bit (+0.0220, t = 9.0, all periods positive), so the signal lives in the recent range rather than the 5-day average. I'll push the same idea one step shorter, to a 2-day mean, to see whether the effect is concentrated in the most recent range or in the past week.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0580
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0206 (t = 8.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0290, 2023 +0.0174, 2024 +0.0196

Two tests in a row came in below the best (+0.0220 and +0.0206), so I'll stop here and hand in the 3-day version.

What I found: the high-low range does predict underperformance, in the direction the idea states — coins whose daily range is wide over the recent days did worse afterwards. The effect is real and stable across all three sub-periods (+0.0315, +0.018, +0.021), and it survives removal of liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, so it is not just a repackaging of those styles. Two refinements were worth the effort: squaring the range (which measures the *magnitude* of the range, not its average level) added nothing, and averaging over 3 days instead of 5 added about 0.002, which is inside the "good" range. The 2-day version was slightly weaker, so I kept the 3-day version rather than going back to the daily range, which is dominated by a single wide day.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ln().ts_mean(window=3, min_periods=3)</factor>
The idea says a big drop yesterday is bullish, so I'll start with the simplest form: the negative of yesterday's return, which is already comparable across coins (it's a ratio of prices).

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The raw one-day return is fully absorbed by the 1-day reversal style (incremental IC 0.0000), so the bounce has to come from a slower version of the fall — a big drop that was not just the single day's return. I'll measure the drop as the distance from the coin's own 20-day average, which keeps the direction (bigger drop → higher value) and is bounded by price.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0497
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0116 (t = 5.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0147, 2023 +0.0172, 2024 +0.0044

Now the drop measured against the coin's own 20-day average has real incremental content (0.0116, t = 5.4) and the sign is consistent across all three periods, so the effect is not just a single-day artifact. To make the "big fall" reading more robust, I'll square the normalized drop before averaging, so only large relative drops score high — a sharp single day can't dominate the average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0330
